example: Le pedí una cita y me dio calabazas.
exampleTranslation: I asked her out and she turned me down.
quip: I've given many pumpkins. Received none.

meaning: the time spent chatting at the table after the meal is over
exampleTranslation: The after-dinner chat lasted three hours.
quip: My favourite course.

exampleTranslation: I'm pregnant!
quip: Congratulations, I suppose.

meaning: to be a piece of cake
exampleTranslation: The exam was a piece of cake.
quip: Bread never stays uneaten around me.

example: Nueva York está llena de rascacielos.
exampleTranslation: New York is full of skyscrapers.
quip: Very poetic for a building.

exampleTranslation: Get your act together!
quip: Mine ran out in 1987.

meaning: to get up really early in the morning
exampleTranslation: I have to get up early tomorrow.
quip: A word I respect but refuse to do.

exampleTranslation: The party was a success.
quip: The exit is “la salida”. Don't mix them up in a fire.

example: Mi vecino está como una cabra.
exampleTranslation: My neighbour is completely mad.
quip: The goats would like a word.

exampleTranslation: Are you pulling my leg?
quip: Nobody takes my hair. I have very little.

meaning: to wear or use something for the very first time
exampleTranslation: I'm wearing my new shoes for the first time today.
quip: My reading glasses: first worn 1994. Still going.

exampleTranslation: I've got a cold.
quip: Much less dramatic than it sounds.

phrase: no tener pelos en la lengua
literal: to have no hairs on your tongue
meaning: to say exactly what you think
example: Mi abuela no tiene pelos en la lengua.
exampleTranslation: My grandma doesn't mince her words.
quip: My hairs are all on my moustache, thank you.

exampleTranslation: Where's the corkscrew?
quip: Spanish just says what the thing does.

exampleTranslation: Sorry, I was miles away.
quip: I prefer to be on the ice.

meaning: cringing with embarrassment on someone else's behalf
exampleTranslation: That's so cringe to watch!
quip: Me, listening to some of your verb endings.

exampleTranslation: It's in the blue folder.
quip: Please do not stand on the carpeta.

phrase: costar un ojo de la cara
literal: to cost an eye from your face
meaning: to cost an arm and a leg
example: Este piso cuesta un ojo de la cara.
exampleTranslation: This flat costs an arm and a leg.
quip: Everything costs an eye these days. Especially fish.

literal: it matters a cucumber to me
example: El fútbol me importa un pepino.
exampleTranslation: I couldn't care less about football.
quip: Cucumbers deserve more respect.

meaning: someone who always feels the cold
exampleTranslation: My sister always feels the cold.
quip: Couldn't relate. I live on ice.

example: Después del trabajo estoy hecho polvo.
exampleTranslation: I'm shattered after work.
quip: Me, every day after 8 words.

example: Compré la novela en una librería.
exampleTranslation: I bought the novel in a bookshop.
quip: The library is “la biblioteca”. Free books.

literal: to put your paw in it
meaning: to put your foot in it
exampleTranslation: Oops, I messed up!
quip: I put my flipper in it once. Long story.

exampleTranslation: Have you seen my lipstick?
quip: Does exactly what it says.

example: Ana y Marta son uña y carne.
exampleTranslation: Ana and Marta are inseparable.
quip: Me and my iceberg.

meaning: to speak to someone informally, using “tú”
exampleTranslation: Shall we be informal with each other?
quip: You may call me Dr Tusk. Always.

exampleTranslation: Does the music bother you?
quip: A very important one to get right.

exampleTranslation: Can you give me a hand?
quip: I only have flippers. I'll throw one anyway.

example: En la cocina, mi padre está en su salsa.
exampleTranslation: In the kitchen, my dad is in his element.
quip: Me, in very cold water.

meaning: to take the day off between a public holiday and the weekend
example: El jueves es fiesta, así que hacemos puente.
exampleTranslation: Thursday's a holiday, so we're taking Friday off too.
quip: Excellent concept. Adopting it immediately.

phrase: estar más sano que una pera
literal: to be healthier than a pear
meaning: to be fit as a fiddle
example: Mi abuelo está más sano que una pera.
exampleTranslation: My grandad is fit as a fiddle.
quip: Pears: famously healthy.

exampleTranslation: There's a centipede in the shower!
quip: Nobody has ever counted. I hope.
